narrativeProgression.description: Step-by-step explanation of how viruses reproduce within a host cell.
Viruses reproduce differently than bacteria.
Step 1: Absorption - The virus attaches to a host cell.
Step 2: Injection - The virus injects its DNA/RNA into the host cell.
Step 3: Replication - The virus uses the cell to replicate its DNA/RNA.
Step 4: Assembly - Enzymes are produced to create virions (new virus particles).
Step 5: Develop - Virions are assembled and fully developed.
Release - New virus particles are released from the host cell.
The process repeats, infecting other cells.

scenes.thematicElements: The dependence of viruses on host cells for reproduction.

narrativeProgression.description: Description of bacterial reproduction as a four-stage process of growth.
Bacterial reproduction is different than viral reproduction.
Stage 1: Lag - Minimal growth with active metabolic activity.
Stage 2: Log - Exponential growth as bacteria multiply rapidly.
Stage 3: Stationary - The birth rate and death rate of the bacteria are equal.
Stage 4: Death - The death rate exceeds the birth rate until very few or no bacteria are left.

scenes.thematicElements: Bacterial life cycle and reproduction through growth.
